verses.1: And all the soldiers came forward. Also Jochanan son of Zadok, and Zadya son of Hoshea. And all the people, from the youngest to the oldest.
verses.2: And they said to the prophet Jeremiah, “Please stop and rest before us. Pray for us to God, your Lord, for all these people. We have been left behind by many, as your eyes can see.”
verses.3: And Jehovah your God will show us the path we must follow, and what must be done.
verses.4: And Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard what you said. I am praying to the LORD your God according to what you have said. And whatever the LORD will answer to you, I will tell you without any hesitation.”
verses.5: And they said to Jeremiah, “May the LORD truly be our God forever. We will believe if all that Jehovah, your God, sends you to us is true. Then it will be so indeed.”
verses.6: Whether it is good or bad, let us listen to the voice of our God, Jehovah. We send you to Him, so that we may hear His words. This will be beneficial for us, because by listening to the voice of our God, we will be guided.
verses.7: And after twelve days, the words of Jehovah were spoken to Jeremiah.
verses.8: And he called out to Jochanan, son of Karah, and to all the officers in the army. He also called out to everyone, from the smallest to the biggest.
verses.9: And He said to them, “As the LORD God of Israel says: ‘I have sent you there to set up your camp before Him.’”
verses.10: If you will return to this land again, and I will plant you there, then I will not destroy you. I will cultivate the land for you, and I will not destroy you, because I have pacified the evil that I did to you.
verses.11: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon. You should not fear him at all. Let us say, “The LORD has said that I will save you and rescue you from his hands.”
verses.12: And I will show you compassion and mercy. I will bring you back to your land.
verses.13: And if you say, “We will not dwell in this land,” then I will not listen to the voice of Jehovah, your God.
verses.14: And he said, “Not in Egypt, where there is no war, and where no loud noises are heard. There, one will not starve.”
verses.15: And now, listen to what Jehovah says regarding the remaining Jews. As Jehovah, the army of Israel’s God, says: “If you truly want to come out of Egypt and live there.”
verses.16: And there will be destruction, which you fear. There, in the land of Egypt, you will suffer famine. And the evil that you fear will also befall you there. Then Egypt will bind itself to you again, and there you will die.
verses.17: And all those people who set their faces towards coming to Egypt, will die there. They will die from hunger and disease. There will be no survivors or refugees from this evil that I bring upon them.
verses.18: For as Jehovah, the army of Israel’s God, said, “When I shall strike the rulers of Jerusalem with my fury and with my anger, then I will also strike you with my anger when you come out of Egypt. You will become a curse and a reproach to all nations. And you will never again see this place.”
verses.19: The words of the LORD are against you, descendants of Judah. Do not enter Egypt. Know that I will surely judge you today.
verses.20: For they have set it in their hearts, that you have sent me to Jehovah your God, saying, “Pray to Jehovah our God.” And whatever Jehovah our God says, let us do it.
verses.21: And today I will tell you this, and you have not heard it through the voice of Jehovah your God, and for all those who have sent me to you.
verses.22: And now, know that in times of famine and during times of scarcity, they will remain in the place where you desire to live.
